title: [calendar-module 04/15] Seed a calendars system database with default and system calendars
body:
**Blocked by:** #1427, #1599
**Model tier:** high

## Context

Model tier rationale: It creates a new system database, writes schema into the locked Events database with direct SQL, and backfills a relation edge for every existing Event in every tenant, so a defect in the cutover changes persisted data widely and irreversibly.

There is no calendar entity today. The Events system database (`backend/packages/data/src/seed/seedTenDatabases.ts`) has no link to a calendar, and `systemSettings` holds only a name and a time zone. A tenant is a single user (`users_tenant_id_key`, migration `0056_tenants.sql`) whose language is `users.locale` (default `cs`, migration `0025_auth_schema.sql`).

System databases are seeded by `backend/packages/data/src/seed/seedSystem.ts` (for example `seedInboxPipelineInTransaction`, which creates its own system project item and databases), but `seedSystem` returns `already-seeded` for an existing tenant, so every new database or property on an existing tenant needs a per-tenant cutover in `backend/packages/data/src/db/tenantCutoverMigrations.ts`. The Events database is `schema_locked`, so a property can be added to it only by code with direct database access, the way `seedEmailModuleInTransaction` adds `People.emails`. A generic write of a `system`-owned property is rejected with 403 `forbidden` (`assertWritableProperties` in `chokePoint/itemWrites.ts`).

This issue gives the calendar module its first database, `calendars`, with default and system calendars, and gives every Event a calendar. It is the base for assigning new Events (#1761), guarding system calendars (#1778), the timeline (#1717), invitations (#1901) and subscriptions.

Decision: the user's own calendars are `Personal`, `Work`, `Family` and `Health` (Czech `Osobní`, `Práce`, `Rodina`, `Zdraví`), seeded in the tenant user's language (the tenant user's `locale`, `cs` when no user exists yet). `Personal` is the default calendar. The system calendars are `Tasks` (system key `tasks`), `Birthdays` (`birthdays`), `Sleep` (`sleep`) and `Public holidays - Czechia` (`holidaysCz`), all with `kind` `system`. Public holidays are computed by code, not a preset subscription; `kind` `subscription` is only for calendars that follow a custom ICS feed URL.

Decision: an Event gets its colour from its calendar; there is no Event colour property.

Decision: Tasks do not choose a calendar; they always belong to the `Tasks` calendar (the row with system key `tasks` carries the colour, visibility and notification settings of Tasks). No `calendarPreferences` setting is added to system settings.

Shared-file ordering: this issue also waits for #1599 because both edit the same registry, manifest, cutover, route matrix or hook files listed in Touches.

## Task

Load `canonical-keys`, `db-migrations`, `state-writes` and `testing`.

1. Add `backend/packages/data/src/seed/calendarsKeys.ts` exporting `CALENDARS_MODULE_ID = "calendars"`.
2. Add `backend/packages/data/src/seed/seedCalendars.ts` exporting `seedCalendarsInTransaction(client, ...)`. It creates a system project item for the calendar module (like the Email and MCP seeds), then the system database `calendars` with properties (canonical keys): `name` (title, user), `color` (color, user), `notify` (checkbox, user), `hidden` (checkbox, user), `isDefault` (checkbox, user), `kind` (select `own`, `system`, `subscription`; owner system; an empty value means `own`) and `systemKey` (text, owner system). The two system-owned properties use the calendar module id as `ownerProcess`. Lock the schema afterwards.
3. In the same function, add the relation `Calendars.events` (one-to-many: one calendar, many Events) with its single-valued inverse `Events.calendar`. Events is `schema_locked`, and `propertiesStore` refuses to change a locked schema, so write both properties and the relation definition through the raw client in the three steps `transcription/transcriptsCatalogCutoverMigration.ts` uses for `Transcripts.speakers` (property row, `relation_definitions` row, then the property `config` pointing at it), under `LOCK TABLE properties IN EXCLUSIVE MODE`. Put this in one helper used by both the seed and the cutover, so the definitions are identical.
4. Seed the eight rows: `Personal` (#5856D6, default), `Work` (#007AFF), `Family` (#34C759), `Health` (#FF2D55), `Birthdays` (#8E8E93), `Tasks` (#007AFF), `Sleep` (#5856D6), `Public holidays - Czechia` (#34C759). `notify` is true for `Personal`, `Work`, `Family`, `Health` and `Birthdays`, false for `Tasks`, `Sleep` and the holidays; `hidden` is false for all. Names come from the calendar module catalog by locale (add the keys to `backend/packages/data/src/calendar/i18n/cs.json` and `en.json`).
5. Call `seedCalendarsInTransaction` from `backend/packages/data/src/seed/seedSystem.ts`, after the Events changes that the earlier calendar-schema work made in that function (the seed order matters because it edits the same Events database).
6. Add the cutover `backend/packages/data/src/calendar/calendarsCutoverMigration.ts` and register it in `runTenantCutoverMigrations` in `backend/packages/data/src/db/tenantCutoverMigrations.ts`, after the Events properties cutover (#1416). Per tenant, in one transaction, idempotent: create the database, relation and rows if absent (same function as the seed), then give every Event that has no calendar edge (trashed ones included) an edge to the default calendar, in batches of 500 by direct SQL. A tenant without an Events database is skipped. Follow `docs/adr/2026-09-10-app-code-post-migration-steps.md`.
7. Declare the database in `databases` of `backend/packages/data/src/calendar/calendarModuleManifest.ts` (key `calendars`).
8. Add the Events relation display name `property.events.calendar.name` to `backend/packages/data/src/seed/i18n/cs.json` and `en.json`, and the Calendars database, property and select-option names to the calendar module catalog (`database.calendars.name`, `property.calendars.<key>.name`, `property.calendars.kind.option.<option>`).
9. Tests: a fresh Czech tenant has exactly the eight calendars with the listed colours and `notify` values and `Personal` default; an English tenant gets English names; a generic write of `kind` or `systemKey` is 403; the cutover on a tenant seeded earlier creates the database, rows and one edge from every existing Event (also trashed ones) to `Personal`, a second run changes nothing, and another tenant is untouched.

## Touches

- backend/packages/data/src/seed/calendarsKeys.ts (new)
- backend/packages/data/src/seed/seedCalendars.ts (new)
- backend/packages/data/src/seed/seedSystem.ts (one call)
- backend/packages/data/src/calendar/calendarsCutoverMigration.ts (new)
- backend/packages/data/src/db/tenantCutoverMigrations.ts (one registered cutover)
- backend/packages/data/src/calendar/calendarModuleManifest.ts (`databases` entry)
- backend/packages/data/src/calendar/i18n/cs.json
- backend/packages/data/src/calendar/i18n/en.json
- backend/packages/data/src/seed/i18n/cs.json (`property.events.calendar.name`)
- backend/packages/data/src/seed/i18n/en.json (`property.events.calendar.name`)
- backend/packages/data/src/__tests__ and backend/packages/data/src/calendar/__tests__ (new seed and cutover tests)

## Scope

### In scope

- The `calendars` database, its default and system rows, the `Events.calendar` relation, the seed for new tenants, and the cutover that adds all of it to existing tenants and links every existing Event to the default calendar.

### Out of scope

- Assigning a calendar to Events created later: #1761.
- Rules that guard system calendars, colour format and the single default: #1778.
- Trashing and deleting calendars: #1803.
- Subscription URLs and feeds: #1925.
- Generating the content of the Tasks, Birthdays, Sleep and holiday calendars in the timeline: #1717.

## Acceptance criteria

- When a new Czech tenant is seeded, then it has eight calendars with the colours and `notify` values above, `Personal` is the default, and every system row has its system key.
- When the cutover runs for an existing tenant, then it gains the same calendars and every existing Event has an edge to `Personal`; a second run changes nothing.
- When a client sends a generic write of `kind` or `systemKey` on a calendar, then the response is 403.
- When a user of another tenant lists calendars, then no row of this tenant is visible.
